newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Clinton confers with S. Korea's Kim.
newsitem.headline: Clinton confers with S. Korea's Kim.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and South Korean President Kim Young-sam met privately on Thursday night as senior officials from both governments prepared for talks next week with North Korea on the future of the Korean peninsula.

The two leaders met for 35 minutes, according to White House spokeswoman Anne Luzzatto, who said "they discussed the situation in the north ... which President Kim described as being in a very bad way economically."

On Monday, Charles Kartman, a deputy assistant secretary of state, will meet in New York with deputy foreign ministers from the two Koreas to discuss a U.S.-South Korean proposal for four-party peace talks that would eventually also involve China.
The proposed four-party talks aim to replace the armistice of 1953 that ended the fighting -- but technically not the war on the Korean peninsula -- with a formal peace.
